bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose an excise tax on certain institutions of higher education that allow male participation in female intercollegiate athletic programs or events.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 10090 would amend the Internal Revenue Code to impose a new excise tax administered by IRS, directly implicating the Office of Tax Policy and the Tax Exempt and Government Entities division. Treasury and IRS would bear responsibility for defining taxable events, issuing implementing regulations, and managing compliance and enforcement against affected institutions, creating significant administrative burden and legal risk given the contested Title IX landscape.

bills.title: First Time Homebuyer Debt Reduction Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 10084 would create or expand a federal benefit tied to first-time homebuyer debt relief, implicating Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and potentially IRS administration if any debt reduction is structured as a tax-advantaged or excludable benefit. Treasury faces implementation risk in determining whether discharged debt constitutes taxable income and in coordinating with housing finance regulators on program eligibility and compliance frameworks.

bills.title: Affordable Pricing for Taxpayer-Funded Prescription Drugs Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus identified, Treasury's interest here is limited and indirect: the bill targets drug pricing for federally funded research, which primarily falls under HHS and Commerce jurisdiction rather than any Treasury authority. Treasury would monitor it only for potential revenue or tax-expenditure implications if pricing provisions affect pharmaceutical R&D tax credits under the Internal Revenue Code.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate the penalties for sale for use and use of dyed fuel in taxable use.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 10104 directly amends the Internal Revenue Code to remove excise tax penalties administered by IRS under Treasury authority, implicating the Office of Tax Policy and IRS fuel excise enforcement programs. Eliminating these penalties risks undermining the dyed fuel regime's compliance mechanism, potentially enabling tax-advantaged fuel to enter taxable markets without adequate deterrence and eroding highway and related trust fund revenues.

bills.title: AI Tax and Work Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: The Ways and Means referral gives Treasury jurisdiction over any tax provisions in the bill, likely touching IRS administration of credits, deductions, or penalties tied to AI-related workforce or income reporting rules. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to define "AI" for tax purposes and enforce any new compliance requirements without clear statutory guardrails.

bills.title: Presidential Tax Accountability and Audit Integrity Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 10060 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service, which sits within Treasury, by mandating audit procedures specifically tied to presidential tax returns under IRS authority. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential IRS resource allocation, legal challenges to mandatory audit requirements, and the precedent of legislatively overriding existing IRS examination discretion.

bills.title: Visitable Inclusive Tax credits for Accessible Living (VITAL) Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: The VITAL Act would create or expand tax credits tied to accessible housing modifications, directly implicating the Internal Revenue Code and IRS administration under Treasury's purview. Treasury's implementation risk centers on defining eligible expenditures, preventing fraudulent claims, and estimating the revenue cost for Joint Committee on Taxation scoring purposes.

bills.title: ABLE MATCH (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship) Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9801 would create a federal matching contribution for ABLE account deposits made by low-income eligible individuals, directly implicating IRS authority under IRC Section 529A and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, which administers the ABLE program's regulatory framework. The matching mechanism would require Treasury and IRS to design new contribution verification, income eligibility, and distribution rules, creating significant administrative build-out and potential compliance risk.

bills.title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7147 funds government operations and may carry continuing appropriations riders that affect Treasury's Office of Management and Budget-coordinated budget authorities, including IRS operations and Fiscal Service payment systems. Treasury's implementation risk centers on ensuring uninterrupted disbursement functions and tax administration continuity within the funding constraints and any anomaly provisions embedded in the continuing resolution.

bills.title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Appropriations.
bills.nexus: Treasury's nexus here is limited but real: the bill funds DHS components such as CBP and the Secret Service, the latter of which operates under a protective and investigative mandate that intersects with Treasury's legacy authorities over financial crimes and counterfeiting. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs should monitor funding levels for any provisions affecting the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's information-sharing relationships with DHS, as well as any riders that could alter Secret Service jurisdiction or resources in ways that create implementation gaps for Treasury-coordinated enforcement programs.

bills.title: Buying American Cotton Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7230 falls within Treasury's purview because the Ways and Means Committee's jurisdiction over tariffs and trade policy intersects with Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and the Office of International Affairs, both of which administer trade-related sanctions and coordinate on import preference regimes. The implementation risk centers on potential tariff schedule modifications or procurement financing rules that Treasury's Office of Tax Policy may need to score, and any country-of-origin enforcement mechanism could implicate Customs and Border Protection's revenue collection functions, which Treasury oversees.

bills.title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 139.
bills.nexus: Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence (TFI) and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) both depend on DHS appropriations coordination for joint counter-terrorism and anti-money-laundering operations, making funding levels in this bill directly relevant to interagency program continuity. If enacted without adequate cross-agency transfer authorities or with restrictive riders, Treasury faces implementation risk in sustaining shared border security finance programs and illicit finance intelligence-sharing pipelines with DHS components such as HSI.

bills.title: Rural Veterinary Workforce Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2398 falls within Treasury's purview because referral to Ways and Means signals a tax-based mechanism, likely involving income exclusions, deductions, or credits tied to veterinary loan repayment or workforce incentives in rural areas. IRS would bear implementation responsibility for any new tax expenditure, requiring rulemaking, revenue scoring coordination with JCT, and potential interaction with existing educational tax provisions.
